answer: In the attestation graph, trust propagates from anchored participants through bounded random walks, so a vertex’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than self-asserted identities. A sybil cluster with few edges to honest participants has low conductance: its walks rarely escape, and min-cut bounds limit the voting weight it can inherit. A spiral of reciprocal attestations or copper-colored labels cannot raise that bound without adding genuine external connections.
